artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan: slow-bucket gate split for the 600s foreground ceiling, batch-gate-pending marker plus entry guards replacing the advisory deferral directive, generalized contention tagging, and a dispatch watchdog over the existing strand probe.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/dispatch-strand-probe.sh already implements the heartbeat-based dispatch-strand detector that a stall-detection design would otherwise propose building: a read-only, fail-closed probe classifying one task's dispatch live/stranded/unknown from a three-signal conjunction (task-lock.sh heartbeat staleness, task-directory artifact quiescence, commit quiescence), explicitly rejecting process-descendant walks and system load as signals. Its three consumers (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's stranded_suspected, skill-orchestrate Move 3, reconcile-task-status.sh's demotion gate) all invoke it at or after postflight, which is downstream of the dispatch returning. The general shape worth remembering: when a detector seems missing, check whether it exists but is sited downstream of the event it must detect the absence of -- the fix is then an invocation site, not a new detector.

A new orchestrator runtime marker file placed under specs/.orchestration/ inherits wholesale gitignore coverage (specs/.gitignore's **/.orchestration/ rule) and therefore needs NO new ephemeral class. A new top-level specs/.<name> marker instead costs four coordinated surfaces: a class member in scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh (the single canonical definition), a .gitignore entry under the core manifest's provides.root_files, an orchestrator-runtime-files.md Consumer Repo Setup update, and a change to the test pinning those two to each other (check-runtime-file-tracking.sh is gate 14, so the omission is gate-visible). Prefer the .orchestration/ siting for any session-scoped per-invocation marker.
